topics.name: Tools
topics.description: Defining functions the model can request.
notes: - Tool 是模型可以请求调用的函数，由名称、描述和参数 schema 组成。
"""Get the current weather for a city."""
- docstring 会作为工具描述发送给模型，决定模型何时以及如何调用，要写清楚。
- 参数的类型注解会生成参数 schema。

topics.name: Agent Loop
topics.description: How an agent alternates between model calls and tool calls.
notes: - 模型收到消息后，要么直接回答，要么返回带 tool_calls 的 AIMessage。
- 模型本身不执行工具，由 agent 运行时执行，并把 ToolMessage 追加回对话。
- 重复上述过程，直到模型不再请求工具并给出最终回答。
- 限制最大循环次数，避免死循环。
- 工具出错时返回清晰的错误信息，模型才有机会修正参数。

questions.title: What does this code print?
questions.explanation: The tool name defaults to the function name, and invoke() takes a dict of arguments and returns the function result.

questions.title: Fill in the method that makes the model aware of the tools.
questions.codeSnippet:
model_with_tools = model.______([add])
ai_msg = model_with_tools.invoke("What is 2 + 3?")
print(ai_msg.tool_calls)
questions.explanation: bind_tools attaches tool schemas to the model so it can return tool_calls in its AIMessage.

questions.title: Which parts of a tool definition are described to the model?

options.text: The full source code of the function

questions.explanation: The model only sees the name, description and argument schema. The implementation stays in your application.

questions.title: Which message type carries a tool's result back to the model?
questions.explanation: ToolMessage holds the output of a tool call and is linked to the request by tool_call_id.

questions.title: The final model call is rejected by the provider. What is wrong?
questions.codeSnippet:
ai_msg = model_with_tools.invoke(messages)
messages.append(ai_msg)
for call in ai_msg.tool_calls:
    result = tools[call["name"]].invoke(call["args"])
    messages.append(ToolMessage(result))
final = model_with_tools.invoke(messages)

options.text: The ToolMessage has no tool_call_id linking it to the request
ai_msg must not be appended to messages
A model cannot be invoked twice
Tools cannot be stored in a dict

questions.explanation: Use ToolMessage(content=result, tool_call_id=call["id"]). The AI message with tool_calls must stay in the history.

questions.title: Why should an agent loop have a maximum number of iterations?

options.text: To prevent endless loops and runaway cost when the model keeps requesting tools
Because models can only call a tool once
To make tool results more accurate

questions.explanation: Without a limit a confused agent can loop indefinitely, consuming time and tokens.

questions.title: Why does the docstring of a function decorated with @tool matter?

options.text: It is only for human readers and is ignored by the framework
It becomes the tool description the model uses to decide when and how to call the tool
It is executed when the tool is called

questions.explanation: The name, description and argument schema are sent to the model. A clear docstring improves tool selection.

questions.title: When a model decides to use a tool, what actually happens?

options.text: The model runs the Python function itself inside the provider
The model returns an AIMessage with tool_calls; your application or agent runtime executes the tool and sends the result back
The model downloads the function from LangSmith

questions.explanation: The model only requests a call by name and arguments. The runtime runs the tool and appends a ToolMessage so the model can continue.
